topic: India at the UN Security Council
hook: India rejects a UN Security Council seat *without veto*
hook_b: Would you take a UNSC seat without veto power?
tldr: At UN reform talks India said it will not accept 'second-class' permanent seats and that veto cannot stay with the P5 alone.

beats.what: India rejected UN Security Council reform that leaves out veto rights, calling such seats 'second-class' (India Weekly, Khmer Times).
beats.why: Times of India reports India said the veto cannot be restricted to the P5 in a reformed council. News India Times says India wants text-based reform and rejects piecemeal veto fixes.
beats.care: It decides how much say India gets on war, sanctions and shipping. Separately, India's 2028-29 UNSC campaign leads with AI and maritime security (NDTV).

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: India's position, per the reports: no permanent seat without veto, and no veto kept only by the P5. Some outlets headline it as India backing veto for all members; the Times of India line is the narrower one. India is also campaigning for a non-permanent UNSC seat for 2028-29.

cards.q: Should India accept a permanent UNSC seat without veto power?
opts: Yes, take it and push for veto later
Push for veto for all members
UNSC is outdated, build new bodies

learn.t: The P5 are the US, UK, France, Russia and China, the five permanent members who each hold a veto over UNSC decisions.

watch: The next round of UN reform talks.
